title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Rías Baixas and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show Rías Baixas DO, sometimes a sub-zone like Val do Salnés, and the grape. Rías Baixas Albariño means 100% Albariño; Rías Baixas Salnés, Condado do Tea or Rosal may be blends. Barrica means oak-aged. Most wines are released young, within a year of harvest.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Albariño is Galicia's seafood wine: pulpo a la gallega, octopus with paprika and olive oil, mussels, clams, scallops, razor clams, oysters and grilled fish. Galicia's seafood is famous across Spain. Serve at 8 to 10 degrees. Cambados holds an Albariño festival every August.

steps.prompt: Which Galician dish is a classic match for Albariño?
steps.explanation: Octopus with paprika suits Albariño's acidity and salinity.

steps.body: Across the Miño river, in Portugal, the same grape is called Alvarinho and makes the wines of Monção e Melgaço.

steps.prompt: Most Rías Baixas Albariño is released young.
steps.explanation: Yes, usually within a year of harvest.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show the grape, sub-zone and sometimes barrica
Albariño suits octopus, shellfish and grilled fish
